title and abstract.summary: This study quantified body size variation in the species Halictus ligatus across three different urban cities and compared the variation between bees residing in these locations. This study measured the body size variation (head width and intertegular distance) in female Halictus ligatus across three different Midwestern United States cities and assessed the relationship between this body size and temperature.

introduction.summary: This study quantified and compared body size variation in the facultatively eusocial sweat bee species, Halictus ligatus, across three distinct Midwestern cities to determine if body size variation patterns were conserved or diverged among these urban landscapes. This study measured the body size variation in the sweat bee Halictus ligatus across populations sampled from three different cities in the Midwestern United States (Chicago, Detroit, and Saint Louis), and investigated how climate factors might influence this variation. methods.summary: The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of 240 Hylaeus ligatus females collected from community gardens in three Midwestern United States cities. The study measured the head width and intertegular distance of female Hylaeus ligatus to assess their relationship with overall body size and to compare these measurements across three different urban populations.
